questions.q: What was the original ask that kicked off this entire ten-lesson project?
options: Jaffle Shop's Ops Manager wanted one trustworthy customer list, instead of scattered, inconsistent spreadsheets
A request to build a full data warehouse for all of Jaffle Shop's data
A request to migrate Jaffle Shop off Snowflake entirely
A request to build a Power BI dashboard of order history
questions.explain: Lesson 1 opened with the Ops Manager's frustrated complaint about scattered, inconsistent customer data and a request for one trustworthy list — everything built in Lessons 2-9 served that one ask.

questions.q: According to this wrap-up, what matters more to a hiring manager or real stakeholder than which specific dbt command was typed?
options: The transferable skills underneath — requirements clarification, disciplined layering, and testable trust
Whether dbt Cloud or dbt Core was used
The exact Snowflake warehouse size chosen
How fast the dbt build command ran
questions.explain: The lesson's skills table explicitly separates the tool-level skill from the underlying transferable skill, arguing the latter is what actually matters to someone evaluating the work.

questions.q: Which of these was explicitly left OUT of this Beginner capstone's scope, on purpose?
options: Order history, payment totals, an intermediate model layer, and CI/CD
A staging model and a mart model
A dbt source declaration
not_null and unique tests on customer_id
questions.explain: The project stayed deliberately scoped to one source, one staging model, and one mart model — order/payment data, intermediate models, and CI/CD were all explicitly out of bounds, per Lesson 1's scoping.

questions.q: What does the Intermediate capstone add, according to this lesson, that the Beginner project deliberately avoided?
options: raw_orders and raw_payments join in, an intermediate layer appears, and the mart model starts doing real business logic
A switch from Snowflake to a different data warehouse
A move from dbt Core to dbt Cloud
A requirement to stop using tests entirely
questions.explain: The Intermediate project is where orders and payments join into the customer data, an intermediate model layer becomes necessary, and the mart model finally stops being a near-pass-through of staging.

questions.q: Is the Beginner project's narrow scope something to apologize for, according to the lesson?
options: No — it was the correct scope for the actual request, and scoping down is as real a skill as scoping up
Yes — a real analytics engineer should always build the largest possible project
Yes — the project should have included order history from the start
The lesson doesn't address scope at all
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly frames the narrow scope as a deliberate, correct choice matching the actual Lesson 1 ask, not a shortcut or limitation.
